tree.t: Incidental abdominal aneurysm on CT or MRI

note:
Intervals are for the first follow-up and can change with growth rate, comorbidity, and life expectancy. Consider earlier referral at any size for rapid growth or symptoms.
* Lower thresholds: renal artery aneurysm 1.5–2 cm (or ≥ 1 cm with uncontrolled hypertension); splenic artery aneurysm in women of childbearing age or cirrhosis; pancreaticoduodenal aneurysms at any size.
cite: Khosa F et al. Managing Incidental Findings on Abdominal and Pelvic CT and MRI, Part 2: White Paper of the ACR Incidental Findings Committee II on Vascular Findings. J Am Coll Radiol. 2013;10(10):789-794.
